claim: Choose Amazon SQS when you need message-level ack/fail semantics and a visibility timeout: SQS deletes acked messages and redelivers failed messages after a configured visibility timeout.

evidence.quote: Messaging semantics (such as message-level ack/fail) and visibility timeout. For example, you have a queue of work items and want to track the successful completion of each item independently. Amazon SQS tracks the ack/fail so the application doesn’t have to maintain a persistent checkpoint/cursor. Amazon SQS will delete acked messages and redeliver failed messages after a configured visibility timeout.

claim: Choose Amazon SQS when load changes from occasional spikes or business growth and each buffered request can be processed independently, because SQS scales transparently without provisioning instructions from you.
question: When should you use SQS instead of Kinesis Data Streams for unpredictable load?

evidence.quote: Using the ability of Amazon SQS to scale transparently. claim: Kinesis Data Streams offers streaming tables for Apache Iceberg on Amazon S3 Tables and Amazon S3 general-purpose delivery in source data format. Both are available for streams in On-Demand Advantage and On-Demand Standard modes.

evidence.quote: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams offers two features: streaming tables for Apache Iceberg on Amazon S3 Tables, and Amazon S3 general-purpose delivery in source data format.
